title: driver/instruction.json (what the framework is asking the engine to do now)
description: The one outstanding instruction for a driven session, under .dabbler/runs/s<N>/driver/instruction.json. Written only by the driver and replaced whole each time it issues the next one; the engine reads it and answers with the file `answer_schema` names, through the verb `answer_command` spells out. Four kinds and no fifth: `step` asks for work, `rejection` sends an answer back with the reasons it was refused, `interrupt` is the driver having ended an invocation and saying why, `done` says the session is over and nothing more is expected. Every answer the driver acts on is JSON against a schema; the prose an engine writes is for people and the driver never reads it.

schema_version.description: Frozen at v1. A reader that finds any other value refuses the file rather than interpreting it.

seq.description: Monotonic per session. An answer names the seq it answers, so a stale answer cannot be mistaken for the current one.

step_id.description: The work-plan step this instruction is about. Required on `step` and `rejection`; an `interrupt` carries it when the engine is being pointed back at a step.

ask.description: What to do, in words for the engine. Required on `step`.

reasons.description: Why the previous answer was refused, or why the invocation was ended. Required on `rejection` and `interrupt`; each entry is one mechanical reason, never a summary.

round.description: On a `rejection` that carries a verifier's findings: the round they came from, so the disposition can name it.

answer_schema.description: Which answer this instruction expects, by the schema it must validate against. Required on every kind but `done`.

answer_command.description: The `dabbler session ...` command line that writes the answer -- the engine never writes the ledger directly. Required on every kind but `done`.
